You and two friends invest one lakh each. Only one gets rich. Meet Ravi, Meena and Karthik. The year is 2006.
Ravi puts his money in a fixed deposit. Safe. Meena buys gold, like her mother told her. Karthik buys a Nifty index fund, a slice of India's top fifty companies.
Then 2008. The market crashed. Karthik's money had grown to one point five lakh. In one year, it fell to seventy four thousand. Everyone laughed. Ravi slept peacefully.
But Karthik didn't sell. And Meena's gold went nowhere from 2012 to 2015. So who won after twenty years? Guess before I tell you.
Ravi. Three point nine lakh. Safe, but slow, and his interest was taxed every year.
Karthik. Five point eight lakh. Almost six times his money, even after the crash. And that's before dividends.
Meena. Sixteen point nine lakh. Almost seventeen times. Gold won, and nobody saw it coming.
Here's the lesson. No asset wins every time. The next twenty years could flip. Split the money three ways? Eight point nine lakh, with no guessing.
